items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: we recorded with a singer, a girl by the name of Kay Penton.

ctx.x: So most of the guys -- he had to pay out of his pocket, because this was above scale, but he couldn't pay Miles enough so Miles would just come in and play any way, but he wouldn't accept the money. So wait a minute. Tad paid me, gave me a check one night for my salary, and it so happened that my wife worked at the bank that he wrote this check on, and I knew what he had in the bank. I think he had about $12.00 in his account, and he gave me a check at this time for $125.00, which was a lot of money then. And I…

know what you have in the bank. He said, but don't tell the other guys. But it was a great band. We recorded, and we had -- we recorded with a singer, a girl by the name of Kay Penton. who was a beautiful singer. She was -- I think she was married to Slam too. We recorded 'What's New' -- we did quite a few recordings with Kay Penton. I don't know whether you've ever heard of her. Tremendous records. I don't think she's singing now.

But as I said, this was the first time -- I think this was before Dave Bontour was doing with the Peggy Lee thing, you know, with the guitar lead. We did it, you know. So -- but I think they might reissue this record --
